reports.title: IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard Plus (SDDS Plus)
reports.description: Highest tier of the IMF Data Standards Initiatives, established 2012. Builds on the SDDS with nine additional data categories (sectoral balance sheets, general government gross debt, and others) and stricter coverage, periodicity and timeliness requirements. Adherents publish an enhanced National Summary Data Page monitored on the Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board. Sits beside the existing imf-sdds and imf-e-gdds nodes as the third rung of the same initiative.
reports.cadence_note: A standard, not a periodical: revised rarely (legal text amendments). Nominal releases_per_year matching the existing imf-sdds/imf-e-gdds convention so the pulse reads as near-static.

reports.title: ASEAN Community Statistical System (ACSS)
reports.description: Regional statistical cooperation framework established 2011 under the ASEAN Framework of Cooperation in Statistics. Comprises the national statistical systems of the ten ASEAN Member States plus relevant sectoral bodies; harmonises concepts, definitions and classifications and produces comparable regional statistics via the ASEAN Statistical Indicators and the ASEANstats portal. ASEANstats (ASEAN Secretariat Statistics Division) is its technical arm.
reports.cadence_note: A standing framework, not a titled release: no releases_per_year on purpose, so it renders as a standing instrument (hollow), same as statutes.

reports.title: APEC Statistics (StatsAPEC)
reports.description: APEC's statistical databases (Key Indicators Database and Bilateral Linkages Database), compiling comparable economic and trade indicators across the 21 APEC member economies from national statistical offices and international sources. Its glossary names each economy's source agency, including Chinese Taipei's DGBAS.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7): a nominal releases_per_year so the pulse rate reads as continuous rather than one-off.

reports.title: Central Bureau of Statistics (Sudan)
reports.description: Sudan's national statistical office and the agency behind Sudan's GDDS/e-GDDS metadata on the IMF DSBB (posted 19 August 2003; no NSDP ever launched). Institutional core node. STALE URL, flagged 2026-08-22: cbs.gov.sd does not resolve in DNS; the agency's e-GDDS metadata on the IMF DSBB remains the durable public record.
reports.cadence_note: No releases_per_year on purpose: the agency's own portal is down (2026-08-22) and no current publication cadence can be attested; renders as a standing entry.

reports.title: Statistics Mauritius
reports.description: The national statistical office of Mauritius, under the Statistics Act 2000. Maintains the National Summary Data Page for the IMF data standards; Mauritius graduated from GDDS (participant since 21 September 2000) to SDDS on 28 February 2012 as the 70th subscriber, and adhered to SDDS Plus on 16 March 2026 as the first African country. Institutional core node; portal verified live 2026-08-22 (July 2026 CPI and tourism releases).
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7): a nominal releases_per_year so the pulse rate reads as continuous rather than one-off.

reports.title: Statistics Sierra Leone (Stats SL)
reports.description: Sierra Leone's national statistical office. GDDS participant since 29 May 2003; implemented the e-GDDS by disseminating a National Summary Data Page on 8 December 2016, in the first wave of countries to do so. Institutional core node; portal verified live 2026-08-22 (June 2026 CPI, 2026 census content).
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7): a nominal releases_per_year so the pulse rate reads as continuous rather than one-off.

reports.description: Afghanistan's national statistics agency (successor to the Central Statistics Organization). Institutional core node; nsia.gov.af verified reachable 2026-08-22 (site live, publication cadence not attested).

reports.description: Yemen's national statistical office. Behind Yemen's GDDS/e-GDDS metadata on the IMF DSBB (posted 26 April 2001; no NSDP). reports.title: Central Bureau of Statistics (Syria)
reports.description: Syria's national statistical office. Behind the Syrian Arab Republic's GDDS/e-GDDS metadata on the IMF DSBB (posted 12 December 2007; no NSDP). Institutional core node. URL NOTE, 2026-08-22: the agency's own domain cbssyr.sy is COMPROMISED (redirects to a spam campaign) and cbssyr.org is stale/repurposed — neither is linked; the IMF DSBB e-GDDS participant table is used as the durable public record instead.

reports.title: Central Statistical Organization / Authority of Statistics and GIS (Iraq)
reports.publisher: Authority of Statistics and Geographic Information Systems
reports.description: Iraq's national statistical office (COSIT — the Central Statistical Organization, renamed the Authority of Statistics and Geographic Information Systems). Behind Iraq's GDDS/e-GDDS participation (metadata posted 15 December 2009; e-GDDS NSDP not yet disseminated per the IMF's 2025 Article IV). Deliberately NOT a combined CSO+CBI node — the Central Bank of Iraq stays separate. Institutional core node; cosit.gov.iq verified live 2026-08-22 (site updated 2026-08-20).
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7): a nominal releases_per_year so the pulse rate reads as continuous rather than one-off.

dependencies.basis: Compiled and disseminated under SDDS coverage/periodicity/timeliness requirements. IMF 2023 Annual Observance Report: 'Indonesia subscribed to the SDDS on September 24, 1996, and met all the SDDS requirements on June 2, 2000.' Quote raw-verified 2026-08-22.

Bank Indonesia's BOP/IIP statistics are SDDS external-sector data categories on Indonesia's NSDP. 2023 Observance Report: 'Indonesia displayed the SDDS-prescribed components on its NSDP... the Data Template on International Reserves and Foreign Currency Liquidity, External Debt, and International Investment Position.' Raw-verified 2026-08-22.

BPS CPI meets SDDS real-sector requirements (monthly, one-month timeliness). 2023 Observance Report: 'Indonesia met the SDDS requirements for coverage for all data categories... Indonesia's data dissemination was punctual against its ARC for all data categories.' Raw-verified 2026-08-22.

BPS is an ACSS member statistical system and hosted/chaired ACSS13. Joint Media Statement: 'The Thirteenth Session of the ASEAN Community Statistical System Committee (ACSS13), hosted by BPS Statistics Indonesia, was held on 22 to 24 November 2023. The Session was chaired by Ms. Amalia Adininggar Widyasanti, Acting Chief Statistician of BPS Statistics Indonesia.' Raw-verified 2026-08-22.

Core BPS series are supplied to ASEANstats under ACSS data-collection arrangements. ASEANstats: 'ASEANstats is also the technical arm of the ASEAN Community of Statistical System (ACSS)... Harmonization of ASEAN statistics - standardization of concepts, definitions, classifications, and approaches.' Raw-verified 2026-08-22.

Taiwan is not an IMF member and cannot subscribe, but DGBAS maintains a DSBB organised exactly to the SDDS framework: 'The DSBB/DGBAS provides information on the real, fiscal, financial and external sectors of the Republic of China about the Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS), which was established by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in 1996...' Raw-verified 2026-08-22.

DGBAS: 'National accounts statistics, representing the nationwide economic status, is compiled according to System of National Accounts (SNA) 2008, published jointly by United Nations, World Bank, International Monetary Fund, Organization of Economic Cooperation and Development, Commission of the European Communities.' Raw-verified 2026-08-22.

The Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) disseminates BOP statistics under an SDDS-aligned structure: 'The major changes in the compilation methodology of BOP statistics and the data sources shall be released in advance in a bulletin and under the Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS) on the official website of the CBC.' Raw-verified 2026-08-22.

Chinese Taipei is an APEC member economy (1991) and DGBAS series appear in the StatsAPEC databases; the StatsAPEC glossary names 'Chinese Taipei's Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics' with a link to nstatdb.dgbas.gov.tw as a source. Raw-verified 2026-08-22.

The Philippines subscribed to the SDDS on 5 August 1996 and met all specifications on 17 January 2001 (IMF DSBB subscription table row 'Philippines | 5-Aug-1996 | 19-Sep-1996 | 17-Jan-2001', raw-verified live 2026-08-22). PSA series are disseminated under SDDS requirements via the NSDP.

IMF 2025 Article IV: 'Philippines subscribes to the Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS) since August 1996 and publishes the data on its National Summary Data Page.' Raw-verified 2026-08-22 (IMF eLibrary).

BSP external-debt statistics form part of the Philippines' SDDS external-sector categories; the DSBB summary methodology states the data 'are generally compiled in accordance with the concepts and methodology set out in the latest External Debt Statistics: Guide for Compilers and Users published in 2014, and IMF's BPM6'. Raw-verified 2026-08-22.

PSA is an ACSS member system; it co-chaired ACSS15 and holds the 2026 chair. Joint Media Statement: '...with Ms. Minerva Eloisa P. Esquivias, Deputy National Statistician of Philippine Statistics Authority as the Co-chairperson. ... We welcomed the ACSS Chairship of the Philippines in 2026.' Raw-verified 2026-08-22.

The JSNA and sectoral balance sheets are disseminated under SDDS Plus. IMF 2024 Annual Observance Report: 'Japan adhered to the SDDS Plus on April 18, 2016. ... This report covers observance of the SDDS Plus undertakings by Japan in 2024, in the four dimensions of the SDDS Plus.' Raw-verified 2026-08-22.

Japan's CPI (MIC) is a real-sector data category under SDDS Plus, published via the e-Stat NSDP: 'The data shown in this page correspond to the data described on the International Monetary Fund's Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board (DSBB)' with the Consumer Price Index row attributed to MIC. Raw-verified 2026-08-22.

Statistical Handbook of Japan: 'The Japanese National Accounts (JSNA) had been compiled based on the 1993 SNA (adopted by the United Nations in 1993) since 2000. The 2008 SNA (the latest international standard adopted by the United Nations in 2009) was introduced in 2016.' Raw-verified 2026-08-22. (Replaces a round-1 draft edge whose ESRI quote never mentioned the SNA.)
